rubriker.title: FIDE ratings - November 2026
rubriker._rss_content: The US Chess Championships and the European Club Cup were the most important tournaments of the past month, bringing about a number of changes in the rankings of the world's top players. Magnus Carlsen, Hou Yifan, Yagiz Kaan Erdogmus and Alice Lee top the rankings in their respective categories. Meanwhile, Nihal Sarin entered the world top 20 and Hans Niemann dropped below the 2700 mark.

rubriker.title: November Rating Update: Young Stars Rising Fast
rubriker._rss_content: On FIDE’s November list, U.S. Women’s Champion Rachael Li gained 50 points and 11-year-old Bodhana Sivanandan 31, while Carissa Yip dropped 31. Here are the biggest women’s movers of the past month.

rubriker.title: Challenge The Grand Chess Auto Bots
Jon Speelman: Ya-hoo!
rubriker._rss_content: With the World Championship match in Geneva just over three weeks away, Jon Speelman considers the prospects of defending champion Gukesh Dommaraju and challenger Javokhir Sindarov. He reflects on the demands of a 14-game match, recent form and the importance of preparation, while revisiting Sindarov’s attacking win over Hikaru Nakamura in Saint Louis. Speelman also draws on past Candidates battles to underline the tactical possibilities ahead. | Photo: Nils Rohde / ChessBase

rubriker.title: Komet från Indien besökte Stockholm
rubriker._rss_content: IM Jung Min Seo vann Stockholm Grand Prix på 7 poäng av 8. Ett resultat på 87,5 procent. Men bäst segerprocent i turneringen hade faktiskt den tolvårige indiern Vyom Malhotra […] Inlägget Komet från Indien besökte Stockholm dök först upp på Sveriges Schackförbund .

rubriker._rss_content: I dag starter EM i sjakk for ungdom i Hellas. Mesterskapet har 9 runder og går fram til 12. november 2026. rubriker.title: FIDE Can’t Stay Silent on Donetsk
rubriker._rss_content: FIDE has gone quiet on a Donetsk team in Sochi while Turlov’s new leadership leans on familiar faces. The questions keep rolling in every week post FIDE election. We're taking a closer look at the latest one.

rubriker.title: El broche de oro de Capablanca en la Olimpiada de Buenos Aires
rubriker._rss_content: Las Olimpiadas de Ajedrez dan lugar a historias extraordinarias. La Olimpiada de Ajedrez de 1939, celebrada en Buenos Aires, fue especialmente dramática, pues Alemania invadió Polonia el 1 de septiembre de 1939, cuando el torneo aún estaba en marcha, lo que marcó el inicio de la Segunda Guerra Mundial. En este contexto, es fácil pasar por alto que José Raúl Capablanca, campeón del mundo entre 1921 y 1927, disputó en Buenos Aires su último torneo y su última partida de competición.
